Expense Ratio - Please note that before April 1, 2026, (change in regulations as per 
Reg 66 of SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 2026) what was quoted as TER, the 
closest comparable number is now termed as Base TER. The new terminology i.e. 
Total TER includes base TER as a component and also includes the cost of buying 
and selling securities, the securities transaction tax on the same, statutory levies 
on each expense head under Base TER i.e. GST on commissions, operating 
expenses (like RTA fees, custody charges etc.), management fees etc. Finally, 
please note this expense ratio is as of last day of the month but annualised and 
hence does not represent the final annualised total TER, it is subject to fluctuation 
from month to month.
Minimum of Rs. 500/- and in multiples of Re. 1/- thereafter

industry excluding Minor investors) SIP ticket size shall be Rs.250/- SIP restricted to 
three SIP's (only one each in upto three Asset Management Companies). Kindly 
refer to SAI for more details.

WhiteOak Capital Liquid Fund
An Open Ended Liquid Scheme. A relatively Low Interest Rate Risk and Moderate Credit Risk 
Investment Objective
Why to Invest in WhiteOak Capital Liquid Fund ?
The investment objective of the Scheme is to generate optimal returns consistent with moderate 
levels of risk and high liquidity by investing in high quality debt and money market instruments. 
There is no assurance that the investment objective of the Scheme will be achieved.
The Scheme focuses on short term deployment of funds.
The fund endeavors to generate optimal returns with high level of liquidity, minimal 
volatility & low to moderate credit risk. 
The Scheme invests predominantly in short maturity and highly liquid securities like T-bills, 
Banks CD’s, CPs and NCDs of highly rated corporates etc. with a maximum residual maturity 
of 91 days.
The fund seeks to follow stringent liquidity and credit parameters to optimize the risk￾return proposition for the investors.
The Scheme endeavors to maintain high credit quality portfolio by analyzing the 
fundamental credit strength of issuers using in-house credit model.
